description: This phase of Indian History covers the crucial political events from the outbreak of World War II to the Partition and Independence of India. During this period, the Quit India Movement and the Indian National Army (INA) played decisive roles in dismantling British rule.

sections.title: World War II and Initial Responses
sections.description: The outbreak of World War II and the Indian National Congress's reaction to the British government dragging India into the war without Indian consent.

key_concepts.explanation: A proposal made by Viceroy Lord Linlithgow in 1940, which for the first time acknowledged the demand for a Constituent Assembly and offered Dominion Status to India.
A limited, non-violent protest initiated by Mahatma Gandhi to affirm the right to freedom of speech and to protest against the August Offer.

historical_events.significance: Congress resigned from Provincial Governments in protest against India's unilateral involvement in World War II by the British.
Promised Dominion Status, but was rejected by both the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League.

key_associations.extra_info: He was chosen by Gandhi as the first person to offer Individual Satyagraha; Jawaharlal Nehru was the second.

important_facts.fact: Following the resignation of the Congress ministries, the Muslim League, supported by B.R. Ambedkar, celebrated December 22, 1939, as the 'Day of Deliverance'.

sections.title: Cripps Mission and Quit India Movement
sections.description: The failure of the Cripps Mission amid the threat of a Japanese invasion, leading to the launch of India's most massive anti-imperialist struggle.

key_concepts.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi famously termed the proposals of the Cripps Mission as 'a post-dated cheque on a crashing bank' because it offered Dominion Status only after the war.
During the Quit India Movement, local shadow governments were established by overthrowing British rule in places like Ballia (Chittu Pandey), Tamluk (Jatiya Sarkar), and Satara (Prati Sarkar).

historical_events.significance: Led by Sir Stafford Cripps, it proposed Dominion Status after the war but was rejected by all major Indian political parties.
Launched at the Gowalia Tank Maidan in Bombay, where Mahatma Gandhi gave the famous 'Do or Die' call.

key_associations.extra_info: Operated a secret radio station from Bombay to broadcast messages and sustain the Quit India Movement after major leaders were arrested.

important_facts.fact: The Quit India Movement is also known as the August Revolution. It largely became a 'Leaderless Movement' because all top leaders were arrested overnight under 'Operation Zero Hour'.

sections.title: Indian National Army and Post-War Crisis
sections.description: Subhas Chandra Bose's armed struggle outside India's borders and the post-war uprisings within the British Indian armed forces.

historical_events.event: Formation of Provisional Government of Free India
historical_events.significance: Established by Subhas Chandra Bose in Singapore, it was recognized by the Axis Powers during World War II.
An unsuccessful attempt by C. Rajagopalachari to resolve the political deadlock between the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League.
Treason trials of INA officers (P.K. Sehgal, Shah Nawaz Khan, Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon) at the Red Fort, Delhi, which sparked massive nationwide protests.
A rebellion by naval ratings of HMIS Talwar in Bombay against racial discrimination and poor food, which severely shook the foundation of British rule.

key_associations.extra_info: He was the lead counsel defending the INA officers, assisted by prominent lawyers like Tej Bahadur Sapru, K.N. Katju, and Jawaharlal Nehru.
Iconic slogans coined by Bose to motivate the soldiers of the Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj).

sections.title: Cabinet Mission and Interim Government
sections.description: The final major attempt by the British to transfer power seamlessly and the formation of India's Constituent Assembly.

key_concepts.explanation: It initially rejected the demand for a separate Pakistan and proposed a weak central government with the grouping of provincial assemblies.
A day (16 August 1946) called by the Muslim League to violently press for the demand of Pakistan, resulting in the 'Great Calcutta Killings' and widespread communal riots.

historical_events.significance: Paved the way for the creation of the Constituent Assembly of India to draft the nation's constitution.
Formed under the leadership of Jawaharlal Nehru; the Muslim League initially boycotted it but joined later in October.

important_facts.fact: The Cabinet Mission consisted of three British cabinet ministers: Lord Pethick-Lawrence, Sir Stafford Cripps, and A.V. Alexander.

sections.title: Partition and Independence
sections.description: The culminating phase of British rule, marking the partition of the subcontinent and the legislative enactment of Independence.

historical_events.significance: British Prime Minister Clement Attlee declared that the British would quit India by 30 June 1948.
Also known as the '3rd June Plan' or 'Dickie Bird Plan', it officially laid out the blueprint for the Partition of India and Pakistan.

polity_articles.provision: Ended British rule in India and provided for the creation of two independent Dominions: India and Pakistan.
polity_articles.details: The Act received Royal Assent in the British Parliament on 18 July 1947.

key_associations.extra_info: He was the chairman of the Boundary Commission tasked with drawing the international borders between India and Pakistan in Punjab and Bengal.

important_facts.fact: Upon Independence on 15 August 1947, Lord Mountbatten became the first Governor-General of independent India, and Jawaharlal Nehru became its first Prime Minister.
